subject.title: fix(openclaw): harden bridge identity and smoke locking

question: Must the new owner-specific smoke-lock format provide mutual exclusion and safe recovery when older Crabline processes use only the canonical lock directory?
rationale: The implementation intentionally maintains two lock representations, but tests and PR discussion must establish whether mixed-version operation is a supported compatibility promise or a coordinated-upgrade boundary.

options.title: Require mixed-version compatibility
options.body: Keep the canonical fence and add focused proof that old and new lockers cannot overlap, recover, or release each other's active ownership.

options.title: Declare coordinated upgrades
options.body: Accept that mixed versions are unsupported, document the operator-visible upgrade requirement, and simplify behavior around that explicit boundary.

options.title: Split the lock redesign
options.body: Land the independent bridge and fsync hardening separately while pausing the ownership-format change for a narrower compatibility review.

recommendation.title: Require mixed-version compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep the canonical fence and add focused proof that old and new lockers cannot overlap, recover, or release each other's active ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and iterated the compatibility-marker and owner-directory design and can best state its intended operational contract.
